SUBJECT: WORK AUGMENTATION AND SUPPORT DURING OFFICIAL TRAVEL, FIELD
WORKS OR SCHEDULED LEAVE OF ABSENCE

DATE:          02 January 2025

In light of the need to maintain continuous and efficient public service operations across
all divisions, this memorandum serves as a directive regarding the work augmentation
procedures to be followed in cases where employees are engaged in fieldwork or official
business travels and scheduled long leave of absence.

Work Augmentation Procedures:
1. Pre-Travel/Fieldwork/Leave Preparation

o Employees who are scheduled for fieldwork, official business or long
duration of leave of absence must coordinate with their immediate
supervisors at least 3 days before departure to discuss delegation of their
key tasks.

o Alist of ongoing projects, deliverables, and deadlines must be shared with
the designated personnel responsible for covering those duties.

o Employees must ensure that critical tasks are addressed before departure
or are adequately handed over for timely completion.

2. Assignment of Designated Personnel

o Supervisors must assign with the approval of the PGDH or the PGADH, a
colleague or team member to temporarily take over the responsibilities of
employees who will be unavailable during the fieldwork or travel period.

o The designated personnel must be briefed on the scope of work to be
covered, including access to necessary tools, files, and contacts.

o Any ongoing communication with external stakeholders or clients should
also be assigned to an alternate point of contact to avoid delays.

3. Remote Work Arrangements (If Applicable)

o In instances where it is possible, employees on official business travel or
fieldwork may be allowed to continue performing certain duties remotely.
Approval for this arrangement must be obtained from their respective
Division Heads.

o Employees must ensure that they have access to the necessary resources
to perform remote tasks and should remain reachable  thru various
communication channels.

4. Reporting and Coordination

o Employees on fieldwork or business trips must maintain regular
communication with their immediate supervisors to update them on
progress and discuss any urgent matters.

o Designated personnel must provide progress reports to the Division Head
on the tasks they are covering to ensure that all responsibilities are being
effectively managed.

5. Accountability

o Both the employee on official business and the designated personnel are
responsible for ensuring that the transition and handling of tasks are
smooth, and that no lapses in service occur.

o Division Heads are responsible for monitoring the execution of tasks by
the designated personnel and addressing any issues or gaps in service
coverage.

This memorandum takes effect immediately. All divisions are required to strictly comply
with the guidelines to ensure seamless operations during instances of employee travel,
field assignments or scheduled leave.
